title: Analysis query tool
subtitle: Prototype. Reads a local snapshot of one site's bundle and warehouse rows.

progress_rate.label: Progress rate
progress_rate.help: Share of sessions that reached checkout_started.

visit_cvr.label: Visit conversion
visit_cvr.help: Visits that placed an order, over visits.

orders_all.label: Orders (all)
orders_all.help: Every order the store recorded, including those without a tracked visit.

bot_share.label: Dead-session share
bot_share.help: Visits with no human signal, over all visits.

buyer_reach.label: Buyers who saw it
buyer_reach.help: Share of visits to this page that bought in the same visit. The order is not attributed to the page.

single_pv_share.label: Single-page share
single_pv_share.help: Sessions that saw only this page.

completion.label: Completion
completion.help: Sessions that reached a journey's last page, over those that started it.

end_buy_rate.label: Bought, at the end
end_buy_rate.help: Of the sessions that reached a journey's last page, the share that bought.

end_rps.label: Revenue per session, at the end

step_pv.label: Sessions with a product view
step_pv.help: Sessions recording a product view at any point, divided by all sessions in this scope. A reach rate, not a step in an ordered funnel.

step_cart.label: Add-to-cart / product-view session count ratio
step_cart.help: Ratio of any-point session counts. The numerator is not established to be a subset of the denominator; this is not a continuation or abandonment rate.

step_checkout.label: Checkout-start / add-to-cart session count ratio
step_checkout.help: Ratio of any-point session counts. The numerator is not established to be a subset of the denominator; this is not a continuation or abandonment rate.

step_buy.label: Buying / checkout-start session count ratio
step_buy.help: Ratio of any-point session counts. The numerator is not established to be a subset of the denominator; this is not a continuation or abandonment rate.

session_conversion.label: Sessions that bought
session_conversion.help: Sessions with at least one order divided by all sessions in the same scope. This is not orders per session.

atc_reach.label: Sessions with an add-to-cart event
atc_reach.help: Sessions recording this event at any point, divided by all sessions in this scope. Not a product-view-to-cart transition.

checkout_reach.label: Sessions with a checkout-start event
checkout_reach.help: Sessions recording checkout_started at any point, divided by all sessions in this scope. Not ordered funnel continuation.

glossary.text: One kept, human visit in the warehouse. Dead sessions (no human signal) are removed before anything is counted.
The bundle's word for a session. Bundle tables and warehouse tables can differ slightly because they filter differently.
Orders over sessions. A session can hold more than one order, so this can be higher than the share of sessions that bought.
Revenue over sessions. The best single number for comparing two segments of different sizes.
One way of splitting sessions: traffic source, returning, buyer, rager or return intent. The values of one segmentation add up to the all row. Never add values across two segmentations.
A total, not a fourth device. Do not add it to desktop, tablet and mobile.
Sessions that bought. Their buying-session rate is 100% by definition; orders per session can exceed 100%. This segment describes buyers, not acquisition performance.
Last touch. The source recorded on the visit, not the first ad the person saw.
Revenue of sessions that clicked the element. Correlational. It does not mean the element caused the order.
Sessions that started on the page. A different denominator from all visits to the page.
A follow-up window after a trigger (for example an abandoned cart). Count only final = 1 rows, or the same chain is counted at each level.
A screening threshold, not proof that a change is or is not real. Inspect both periods, the actual denominator, outcome counts, and coverage. Small cells remain visible.
Completeness must come from source coverage and the reporting calendar, not low volume. Unknown coverage is not a complete week. Partial-week rates can also have a different weekday mix.
Returning-visitor flags changed on 7 September 2026. Do not compare returning shares across that date.

tabs.label: Weekly brief
tabs.question: What deserves attention?
tabs.intro: At most three findings worth reviewing. Each one keeps its comparison, its volume and its limits.

panels.title: This week
panels.question: Did the week move, and in which part of the purchase?

panels.title: Findings
panels.question: What deserves attention?

tabs.label: Channels
tabs.question: Where is on-site value concentrated?
tabs.intro: Last touch. On-site value only: no spend, so nothing here says a channel is or isn't profitable.

panels.title: Traffic sources
panels.question: Which sources bring sessions, and what share of them bought?

tabs.label: Paths and actions
tabs.question: What share of sessions recorded each action, and which paths completed?
tabs.intro: Actions are recorded anywhere in the session. Paths are a separate, ordered page sequence.

panels.title: Event reach
panels.question: What share of sessions recorded each action?

panels.title: Journeys
panels.question: Which of the ranked paths completed less often?

tabs.label: Explain revenue change
tabs.question: How does the revenue change split?
tabs.intro: An accounting split of the observed change, not its causes.

panels.title: Four-factor revenue bridge
panels.question: How much of the revenue change is sessions, buying rate, orders per buyer and order size?

panels.title: Mix and rate
panels.question: Is the buying-rate change a shift in who arrived, or a change inside each group?

tabs.label: Client brief
tabs.question: What will you take to the call?
tabs.intro: Pins are yours. The recommendation line is yours. Tool statements stay separate.

panels.title: Pinned findings
panels.question: What is on the brief?

tabs.label: Site health
tabs.intro: Week by week, is the site taking the traffic it used to, and turning it into the same revenue? Start here, then follow the segment that moved.

panels.title: Weekly snapshot
panels.question: Is this week better or worse than the weeks before it, and which segment moved?
caveats: Site totals come from one tag key's values, which partition every kept session.
Pick one segmentation at a time. Values of different segmentations overlap.
Under Split by buyer, the order rate is 100% by construction.

panels.title: Day by day
panels.question: Was the change one bad day or a steady slide?
caveats: Orders (all) and Revenue (all) include orders without a tracked visit. Visits exclude dead sessions.

panels.title: The month against the lead-in
panels.question: Is the analysis month different from the weeks just before it?
caveats: Pre is the lead-in, first and second are the two halves of the month, and peak overlaps them.

panels.title: Best days
panels.question: Which days carried the month?

tabs.question: Am I OK?

tabs.label: Acquisition
tabs.intro: Which sources, campaigns and ads bring traffic, and what is that traffic worth once it arrives? Ad spend is not in this data, so this is value per visit, not return on spend.

panels.title: Tagged traffic by week
panels.question: Which source, medium or campaign tag is growing, and is it worth the visit?
caveats: (none) is sessions without this tag. Channel is last touch.

panels.title: Channel, entry and device
panels.question: Which channel's visits convert, and where do they land?
caveats: The first and last week can be partial.

panels.title: Campaigns
panels.question: Which campaigns bring volume but no orders?

panels.title: Meta ads
panels.question: Which ad (utm_content) earns per visit, and which only spends?

panels.title: Which tags the platform tracks
panels.question: Why is a tag in the weekly table or left out?

panels.title: Countries on the analysed page
panels.question: Is one country carrying the page's revenue?
caveats: The analysed page only, not the whole site.

tabs.question: Who is coming, and are they worth it?

tabs.label: Journeys
tabs.intro: The five top journeys through page types (home, collection, product page, content) and the five top journeys through specific URLs, each followed to checkout and purchase. Pick a segment to see the same journeys for one kind of visitor, and a week to compare.

panels.title: Top journeys
panels.question: Where do visitors on each top journey drop off, and did it change this week?
caveats: A journey's first node counts sessions that landed on its first page and either stopped there or went to its second page.
Each later node counts sessions that reached it along the journey. The orange stub is sessions that ended the visit or went to a page off the journey.

The top five are ranked by revenue across all visitors, as the trend run ranks them, and keep that rank when you pick a segment. Lanes with fewer than 300 starters are greyed: read their rates as directional.

next.text: Where in the funnel do they drop?

panels.title: Journeys over time, by segment
panels.question: Is a journey getting better or worse, and for which visitors?
caveats: Rates of a segment with few sessions on a journey jump from week to week. Hover a point for its volume.

panels.title: Journeys by week
panels.question: Which journey's numbers moved most since last week?

panels.title: Behaviour cohorts
panels.question: Do visitors who do X buy more often than those who don't?
caveats: journey3 is the first three page classes of the visit, repeats collapsed.
These are descriptions of visitors who did something, not proof that doing it causes buying.

tabs.question: How do visitors move, and which paths make money?

tabs.label: Funnels
tabs.intro: The purchase funnel, week by week: sessions, product viewed, added to cart, checkout started, bought. Narrow it to visitors who landed on one page type, then split it by a segment to see whose funnel moved.

panels.title: Purchase funnel
panels.question: At which step do most sessions drop, and did that step get better or worse?
caveats: A step counts sessions that did it at any point in the visit, so a session can start checkout without a cart add in the data.
Purchased is sessions with an order.

panels.title: Funnel by segment
panels.question: Whose funnel is weakest, and whose moved this week?

panels.title: Funnel steps over time, by segment
panels.question: Which step is trending, and is it one segment or everyone?

panels.title: Step rates by week
panels.question: Which segment's step rate changed most since last week?

panels.title: Funnel by landing page type
panels.question: Visitors who land on which kind of page buy, and is that holding?

panels.title: Funnel sequence
panels.question: How long does each step take, and who skips the cart?
caveats: The analysed page's bundle table: ordered steps, no segments.

tabs.question: Where do visitors drop out on the way to buying?

tabs.label: Pages
tabs.intro: The pages that carry the traffic, the pages visitors land on, and the one page the platform analysed in depth.

panels.title: Top pages by week
panels.question: Which pages take the traffic, and is their revenue per session holding?
caveats: A session that saw the page counts once. Its revenue is the session's, not attributed to the page.

panels.title: Landing pages by channel
panels.question: Which landing pages bounce, and which convert?
caveats: Entry sessions, not all visits to the page.

panels.title: Page reach and buyers
panels.question: Which pages do buyers pass through?

panels.title: The analysed page
panels.question: On the page the platform studied, which segment underperforms?
caveats: Returning flags changed on 7 September 2026. Do not compare returning splits across that date.

panels.title: Pages high-value buyers over-visit
panels.question: Which pages do high-value buyers see more than everyone else?

panels.title: Sister pages
panels.question: Does a similar page earn more per session than the analysed one?

tabs.question: Which pages take traffic, and which convert it?

tabs.label: Elements
tabs.intro: Clicks, scroll and exposure on the analysed page. Revenue on an element is the revenue of sessions that touched it, which shows association, not cause.

panels.title: Tracked elements by week
panels.question: Are clicks on the key elements holding, and do clickers still buy?
caveats: Element revenue is correlational.

panels.title: Every clicked element
panels.question: Which elements get clicks but no revenue?
caveats: Clicking sessions add up across weeks, not across elements: one session can click many elements.

panels.title: Rage clicks
panels.question: Which kind of element frustrates visitors?

panels.title: Scroll depth
panels.question: How far down the page do entry visitors get?

panels.title: Sections seen
panels.question: Which sections do visitors actually see, and do those sessions buy?

panels.title: Where clicks lead
panels.question: After a click, which kind of page comes next?

tabs.question: What on the page earns, and what is broken?

tabs.label: Visitors over time
tabs.intro: What happens after a first visit, an abandoned cart or an email click. Everything here is counted per browser, and one person can use several.

panels.title: Follow-up after a trigger
panels.question: After an abandoned cart or browse, how many come back and buy?
caveats: Only final = 1 rows are counted, so each chain is counted once.
Chains started late in the window have less time to come back.

panels.title: Chains by start day
panels.question: Is recovery steady, or did one day's batch skew it?

panels.title: Return intent by week
panels.question: Do returning visitors with intent convert better, and is that share growing?
caveats: Return intent looks back 30 days on the same browser.

panels.title: 30-day history
panels.question: Do visitors with recent history convert better?
caveats: A buying visit can be labelled bought_before because of its own earlier order in the window. Read bought_before as history, not as a loyal-buyer segment.

panels.title: Email clicks per device
panels.question: Do devices that click several emails buy more?

tabs.question: Do they come back and buy?

tabs.label: Orders and products
tabs.intro: Order values, products and markdowns. Orders here come from the store, so they include orders without a tracked visit.

panels.title: Order value
panels.question: Where do order values cluster, and where does revenue come from?

panels.title: Products
panels.question: Which products carry revenue, and how much of it is discounted?
caveats: An order is filed under its highest-priced line.

panels.title: High-value and marked-down orders by day
panels.question: Is the order mix shifting towards discounts?

panels.title: Product entry pages
panels.question: Which product landing pages convert?

tabs.question: What do they buy, and at what price?

tabs.label: Experiments
tabs.intro: Tests the platform found on the site, how their arms compare, and whether the split looks healthy week by week.

panels.title: Arm readout
panels.question: Which arm is ahead, and by how much?
caveats: This prototype does not test significance or sample ratio. Use the share column to eyeball the split.

panels.title: Arms by week
panels.question: Is the gap stable, or did one week make it?

panels.title: Experiments found
panels.question: Which tests ran, when, and how big were they?

tabs.question: Is the test real, and is it winning?

tabs.label: Verdicts
tabs.intro: The rules the platform ran, the cards it recommends, and the data it could not get.

panels.title: Rules on the analysed page
panels.question: Which rules fired, and on what numbers?

panels.title: Strategy cards
panels.question: Which cards made the cut, and what blocked the rest?

panels.title: Data requirements
panels.question: How much of what the strategies need is available?

panels.title: Requirement detail
panels.question: What exactly is missing?

tabs.question: What does the platform think I should do?

funnel.scope: site event reach in the flow snapshot

journeys.scope: frozen selected paths in flow snapshot

tag_trend.scope: tag population, not interchangeable with flow snapshot

weekly_entry_cube.scope: bundle kept visits; separate population contract

journey_summary.scope: frozen selected paths, derived from journeys

screening.label: Large enough to review, not proof of cause
screening.multipleComparisons: z = inverseNormal(1 - 0.05 / (2*M)); M fixed before ranking

answerRules.claimTemplate: {path}: {completion} completed, {delta_pp} points versus the week of {compare_week}, across {starts} starts.
prohibitedClaims: site-wide largest path without ranking coverage

answerRules.claimTemplate: {source}: {share} of sessions, {rate} of them bought, versus {others_rate} for all other sources ({top2_label} {top2_rate}).
{action}: {current} of sessions, {delta_pp} points versus the week of {compare_week}.

emptyState: No eligible movement found in the loaded coverage. This is not a claim that the site is healthy.
